translation_notes: The walk `for s, p, o in graph.triples((None, None, None))` is `for s, p, o in m{ ?s ?p ?o }`, and each `graph.remove((s, p, o))` / `graph.add((s, p, o))` is `-{ {s} {p} {o} }` / `+{ {s} {p} {o} }` on the graph designated by `@graph graph`. All three terms are bound, so the `-{ }` is an exact removal, not a wildcard.

The graph is rewritten WHILE the lazy `m{ }` iterates it; this is safe on rdflib's in-memory store (the original does the same with `.triples()`), and the check proves it on a fixture where every position of a triple is rewritten.

Faithful quirk kept: a literal that contains the remote location is turned into a URIRef (the substring test `in o` is true of a Literal), which the fixture exercises; a literal with a space would produce an invalid IRI on both sides, so the fixture has none.
Driver: `self` is a SimpleNamespace holding the two locations; the oracle is the mutation of the graph argument (four calls, one of which matches nothing).
optimization_notes: optimized.py: the three copy-pasted blocks (one per position) become one generator that rewrites each term of the triple containing the remote location, then one remove/add when the rewritten triple differs. The original's intermediate add-then-remove of a half-rewritten triple is not reproduced: such a triple still contains the remote location, so it is itself rewritten by its own iteration (graph.triples((None, None, None)) iterates a snapshot), and the final graph is the same; the only divergence would need a local location that itself contains the remote one.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: only the walk is an island, `m{ ?s ?p ?o }(graph)` in place of graph.triples((None, None, None)). The remove and add take the triple as a Python tuple, which no island accepts: `-{ }`/`+{ }` would need the three terms unpacked and re-interpolated, longer than graph.remove(triple)/graph.add(new_triple), so the two calls are kept (reported, as for a pattern received as data).
No exception to the symmetry rule. Almost all the gain is the rereading (care 0.44); the notation saves only the wildcard pattern.
